 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 03.06.2023 passed in MVC.No.4162/2020 by the Court of Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes,
Member, Principal MACT, Bengaluru (for short 'the tribunal').
The appeal is preferred on the premise of exorbitant compensation awarded by the tribunal contrary to the materials placed on record.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
On 29.05.2020 at about 12.00 a.m. the claimant as a pillion rider along with rider was going on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EC-8005.

When they NC:
2024:KHC:14941 reached near Navile gate, on the left side of T.C.Road to go towards Nuggehalli, the rider of another motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EL-2307 came in high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the claimant.
Due to which, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately shifted to the Government Hospital, Channarayapatna and thereafter, to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, where he expended financial expenditure and due to the injuries sustained by the claimant, he filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
3.1 On service of notice, respondent No.2 was placed ex parte.

Respondent No.1 appeared and filed detailed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation, income and pleaded that the accident did not occur due to the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle rather due to the negligence of the claimant himself and also pleaded that the rider of the vehicle did not possess a valid and NC: 2024:KHC:14941 effective Driving Licence, so also,

Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.2 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
3.3 In order to substantiate the issue and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P17.
On the other hand, the respondents neither examined any witness nor got marked any documents.

3.4 On the basis of material evidence produced by the parties, the tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.10,05,000/- along with interest at 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.1 to deposit the compensation within three months.

3.5 Being aggrieved by the exorbitant compensation amount awarded by the tribunal,
the Insurance Company NC: 2024:KHC:14941 is before this Court questioning the said judgment and award and its propriety.
4. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for appellant-Insurance Company that the tribunal awarded exorbitant compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, he seeks to reduce the compensation.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1- claimant vehemently contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation,
which does not call for interference.
Hence, he seeks for dismissal of the appeal.
6. I have heard learned counsel for appellant- Insurance Company and respondent No.1-claimant and perused the impugned judgment and award.
7. The occurrence of accident, involvement of vehicle and injuries sustained by the claimant are not disputed and the same are established by production of Exs.P1 to NC: 2024:KHC:14941 P17.
The Police records depict filing of FIR and laying of chargesheet against the rider of the offending motor cycle, which is not disputed or challenged.
Hence, negligence is rightly attributed as against the rider of the offending motor cycle.

8. Now coming to the age, avocation, income and disability, it is seen that the claimant was aged 47 years as on the date of occurrence of accident and the tribunal applied multiplier at '13', which does not call for interference and the same is retained.
The tribunal has taken the income of the claimant at Rs.20,000/- per month, whereas, the claimant himself has pleaded that he was earning an income of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Therefore, the income assessed by the tribunal is on the higher side and there is no documentary proof produced with regard to income.

Hence, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes Rs.14,500/- per month for the accident of the year 2020 and the same is NC: 2024:KHC:14941 taken as income of the claimant in the absence United India Insurance Co Ltd vs N L Nagaraju on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20691473/

sentences.text:
9. PW.2-Doctor assessed the physical disability to an extent of 55% to the right lower limb and 19%
to the whole body, whereas, the tribunal has assessed the functional disability at 15%.
However, the claimant is not in appeal.
Hence, I do not find any reason to interfere with functional disability of 15% assessed by the tribunal and the same is retained.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.3,39,300/- (Rs.14,500/- x 12 x 13 x 15%) towards loss of future income due to permanent disability as against Rs.4,68,000/-.

10. The tribunal awarded Rs.75,000/- towards pain and agony, Rs.3,07,000/- towards medical expenses (conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges), Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses and Rs.50,000/- towards unhappiness and loss of amenities, which do not call for interference and the same are retained.
NC: 2024:KHC:14941 11.
The tribunal awarded Rs.80,000/- towards loss of income during the treatment and rest period by taking the income at Rs.20,000/- for 04 months.

However, in view of this Court reducing the income from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.14,500/- and taking the income at Rs.14,500/- for 04 months, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.58,000/- (Rs.14,500/- x 4) under this head.

14. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to the reduced compensation of Rs.8,54,300/- as against Rs.10,05,000/- as mentioned in the table below:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and agony 75,000-00 Medical expenses (conveyance, 3,07,000-00 nourishment and attendant charges) Loss of income during the treatment 58,000-00 and rest period Loss of future income due to 3,39,300-00 permanent disability Future medical expenses 25,000-00 Unhappiness and loss of amenities 50,000-00 TOTAL 8,54,300-00 15.
